notes:
350 names mapped. English names follow IOC: Brant Goose, Common Murre, Black-throated Loon, Long-tailed Jaeger, Tundra Swan (Bewick's), Western Barn Owl. Whitethroat and Barred Warbler are now in Curruca, and Shag is Gulosus.

Things to check:
(1) Victorian 'Black Scoter' (n=165-166) is the Common Scoter, Melanitta nigra. It is not IOC's Black Scoter, M. americana.
(2) Keepers used 'Barnacle' loosely (n=96 and n=102, 154 records). One turned out to be a White-fronted Goose (n=101).
(3) Bean Goose (n=17, 109, 110) is left at genus Anser because IOC splits Taiga and Tundra.
(4) Bare Latin epithets need the genus that precedes them in each record: arborea/arboreus (n=70 is unknown; n=71 and n=55 are guesses), alba, cinerea, arvensis, campestris, brachydactyla. In the Heligoland lists, October flocks of 'arborea' point to Woodlark; spring and early autumn birds point to Tree Pipit.
(5) Garbled small-caps headings: Antu1p#/AntHipm = ANTHIDÆ, Ataupip%/AtaupIpm™ = ALAUDIDÆ, Aucipa/Aucipm = ALCIDÆ, BuveE Tit = Blue Tit, BuiackceaP = Blackcap, Buack Repstart = Black Redstart, CHoueH = Chough. Books = Rooks and Bing Ouzels = Ring Ouzels. Check these against the scans.
(6) Compound names (n=137, 138, 140, 295, also 293) may need splitting into separate records.
(7) Unknowns to read from the scans: n=1, 4, 13, 18, 108, 115, 133, 149-150, 198, 214, 241, 333-334, 348.
(8) 'Blue Janet' = Dunnock (n=215-216) is from memory; check it against Swainson.
(9) Exclude escapes and domestic birds from migration analysis: Black Swan (n=170), carrier pigeons (n=291-292), and possibly Red-winged Blackbird (n=24).
(10) Plain 'Buzzard' is mapped to Common Buzzard and 'Brown Wren' to Eurasian Wren, both tentatively.
